standards.name: ICAT Schema
standards.abstract: This standard describes a core scientific metadata model (CSMD)-based schema for describing facilities, instruments, investigations, datasets and datafiles collected at scientific facilities. The research objects are investigations and their associated datasets/datafiles (and related entities such as samples, jobs and data collections) arising from facility-run experiments; the model assumes data recorded as database entities (schema of entities, parameters and types) rather than a single file format. The ICAT Schema is maintained by the ICAT Project and its documentation is generated from the code; it addresses the problem of representing the relationships between facilities, instruments, investigations, datasets, datafiles, users and authorization/grouping constructs and also records how parameters and types relate to entities.

classification.rationale: The source material describes a set of named entities and the relationships between them (a schema diagram / entity-relationship view) and explicitly explains how entities relate to one another (e.g., Facility -> Investigation -> Dataset -> Datafile). This is a directed graph of entities (a DAG) rather than a field-level metadata table or a prose checklist of reporting principles.

Facility.name: Facility
Facility.description: A facility that hosts instruments and supports investigations; central organisational unit in the schema.
Facility.evidence: A Facility can be seen as a set of Instruments.

Instrument.name: Instrument
Instrument.description: An instrument (belonging to a facility) used to produce datasets/datafiles.
Instrument.evidence: A Facility can be seen as a set of Instruments.

Investigation.name: Investigation
Investigation.description: A study or investigation carried out at a facility that groups datasets and relates to samples and other metadata.
Investigation.evidence: Each Facility supports a number of Investigations where there may be a one-to one correspondence between an Investigation and a proposal which is not part of the schema.

Publication.name: Publication
Publication.description: A publication record related to an investigation (the schema notes a one-to-one relation here).
Publication.evidence: A Publication corresponds to exactly one Investigation (which is probably bad modelling -- the Publication should be related to a Study representing the output of that study).

FacilityCycle.name: FacilityCycle
FacilityCycle.description: A period of running for a facility (used to define cycles/sessions of facility operation).
FacilityCycle.evidence: A facility may also make use of FacilityCycles to define a period of running.

Dataset.name: Dataset
Dataset.description: A collection of Datafiles that share something in common; datasets belong to investigations and may be associated with samples.
Dataset.evidence: The Investigation has a number of Datasets that belong to it where each Dataset is made up of a number of Datafiles.

Datafile.name: Datafile
Datafile.description: A physical file with attributes such as length and checksum; the basic stored artefact.
Datafile.evidence: The Datafile is a physical file with a length and checksum whereas the Dataset is a collection of Datafiles with something in common.

DataCollection.name: DataCollection
DataCollection.description: A grouping of individual Datafiles or Datasets of Datafiles which may span Investigations or Facilities; used to represent input/output of jobs.
DataCollection.evidence: In addition there is the notion of DataCollection which groups together individual Datafiles or Datasets of Datafiles which may span Investigations or even Facilities.

Job.name: Job
Job.description: A job that takes an input DataCollection and produces an output DataCollection; related to an application that performs the conversion.
Job.evidence: A DataCollection is used to represent the input to a job and another DataCollection is used for the output. The Job is also related to the Application which converts the input DataCollection to an output.

Application.name: Application
Application.description: An application which converts input DataCollections into output DataCollections (used by jobs).
Application.evidence: The Job is also related to the Application which converts the input DataCollection to an output.

Sample.name: Sample
Sample.description: A sample associated with investigations and datasets (used to clarify the set of samples used and for safety reasons).
Sample.evidence: Samples are associated both with an Investigation to clarify the full set of Samples to be used (partly for safety reasons) and with the Dataset which is related to at most one Sample.

User.name: User
User.description: A user of the system who may be associated with instruments and grouped for authorization purposes.
User.evidence: The first diagram has been simplified by omitting all those entities which have been added to avoid many-to-many relationships. For example an Instrument has many Users and a  User may be associated with many Instruments.

Grouping.name: Grouping
Grouping.description: A grouping of users (used to collect users into groups for authorization and management).
Grouping.evidence: Users are collected together into groups (known here as Groupings to avoid keyword problems) and authorization Rules are associated with these groupings.

AuthorizationRule.name: Authorization Rule
AuthorizationRule.description: An authorization rule associated with groupings to control access.
AuthorizationRule.evidence: Users are collected together into groups (known here as Groupings to avoid keyword problems) and authorization Rules are associated with these groupings.

PublicStep.name: PublicStep
PublicStep.description: A construct to speed up authorization decisions (optimisation to help authorization checks).
PublicStep.evidence: Log is used for call logging and PublicStep is to speed up authorization decisions.

Parameter.name: Parameter
Parameter.description: A parameter attached to entities (parameters have types and are shown in the schema diagram).
Parameter.evidence: In addition all parameters have a ParameterType and all types are related to a Facility.

ParameterType.name: ParameterType
ParameterType.description: The type of a parameter; ParameterType may belong to a facility and is used by parameters.
ParameterType.evidence: In addition all parameters have a ParameterType and all types are related to a Facility.

Type.name: Type
Type.description: Entity types as shown in the second diagram (types are related to a facility and appear on the right of the diagram).
Type.evidence: The second diagram shows those entities (column in the middle of the diagram) with their related parameters in the column to the left of centre and types to the right of centre (where DatafileFormat is here treated as a type.

DatafileFormat.name: DatafileFormat
DatafileFormat.description: A datafile format treated as a type within the schema (an example of a type).
DatafileFormat.evidence: The second diagram shows those entities (column in the middle of the diagram) with their related parameters in the column to the left of centre and types to the right of centre (where DatafileFormat is here treated as a type.

errors.detail: Graph is not fully connected; unreachable node(s) from an arbitrary start

standards.notes: Graph constructed to reflect explicit entity relationships stated in the ICAT Schema page; nodes each include a verbatim evidence quote from the source. The DAG is connected so every node is reachable via edges from the Facility/Instrument/Investigation subgraph.
